rows.speaker: İbn Sînâ
rows.claim: Ibn Sina urges withholding judgment on reports of an arif's prayers bringing rain or healing, averting disasters, or affecting animals, since hidden natural causes may underlie such wonders.
rows.anchor: İbn Sînâ İşârât’ının nihâyetinde “Esrâr-ı Âyât”

rows.speaker: İbn Sînâ
rows.claim: Ibn Sina traces unseen natural effects to psychic constitution, properties of elemental bodies, or celestial forces, associating magic with the first, miracles and saintly wonders with the second, and talismans with the third.
rows.anchor: İbn Sînâ İşârât’ının nihâyetinde “Esrâr-ı Âyât”

rows.speaker: İbn Sînâ
rows.claim: Ibn Sina says denial without proof is as irrational as credulous assent; when a report seems strange, suspend judgment unless there is proof it is impossible, because nature holds many marvels.
rows.anchor: İbn Sînâ İşârât’ının nihâyetinde “Esrâr-ı Âyât”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says Ibn Sina wrongly treated the heavens and celestial bodies as simple, non-elemental, untouchable substances whose lack of rectilinear-motion inclination made them incapable of being torn or corrupted.
rows.anchor: İbn Sînâ teessüf olunur ki ilm-i tabîî nâmına nazariyesinde yanlış bir fikre zâhib olmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı argues that allowing a body's inclination to circular motion while excluding inclination to straight motion is an unsupported contradiction, since direction is accidental to motion and any obstacle needs a separate account.
rows.anchor: Birinin câiz olabildiği bir yerde diğeri de câiz olabilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says stars and their spheres are composed of elemental matter like Earth and can undergo generation and corruption, in accord with the scientific and philosophical views of his time.
rows.anchor: Onlar da Arz gibi ecsâm-ı unsuriyeden mürekkeb ve binâen‘aleyh kevn ü fesâdı kābildirler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given theories that the Moon separated from Earth, a philosopher may read the verse as a past event, but cannot use that reading to deny either the prophetic miracle or a future splitting at the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: Buna göre de وَٱنشَقَّ ٱلْقَمَرُ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Modern science does not deny that the Moon can split; Elmalılı lists internal explosion, external currents, waves, collision, elasticity, or pressure as conceivable mechanisms, while leaving the necessary force undetermined.
rows.anchor: Bugünkü fen Kamer’i bir cism-i esîrî farzetmediği gibi yarılabilmek kābiliyetini de inkâr etmez.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The actual agent is God's power and will; no messenger brings a sign except by God's leave.
rows.anchor: mevzû‘-i bahis olan müessir ise Allah teâlâ’nın kudret ve iradesidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı contrasts the knowledge-and-witnessing nearness disclosed in the Najm account with the volitional nearness manifested in the Moon's splitting at the Messenger's request.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Necm’de “şedîdü’l-kuvâ”nın tâlimiyle istivâdan sonra kābe kavseyni ev ednâ tedellîsinde rü’yet-i âyât ile tecellî eden kurb-i ilmî ve şuhûdî

rows.speaker: Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
rows.claim: Ibn Arabi describes the Moon as an intermediate station between crescent and full Moon: hilal names its appearance, badr its light filling the eye, and mihak its concealment by sunlight.
rows.anchor: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî Fütûhât’ının üç yüz otuzuncu bâbında Hazret-i Muhammediyeden menzil-i Kamer’i marifet hakkında berzahî bir ifade ile şöyle der:

rows.speaker: Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
rows.claim: Ibn Arabi reads the Moon's changing stations as a sign for recognizing the Perfect Human and attaining knowledge of God; its waxing and waning exemplify transitions between the unseen and witnessed realms, and its splitting images manifestation in two forms.
rows.anchor: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî Fütûhât’ının üç yüz otuzuncu bâbında Hazret-i Muhammediyeden menzil-i Kamer’i marifet hakkında berzahî bir ifade ile şöyle der:

rows.speaker: Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
rows.claim: Ibn Arabi cites a Companion report that the Moon split during the Prophet's time after Arabs asked for a sign, and the Prophet told those present to bear witness.
rows.anchor: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî Fütûhât’ının üç yüz otuzuncu bâbında Hazret-i Muhammediyeden menzil-i Kamer’i marifet hakkında berzahî bir ifade ile şöyle der:

rows.speaker: Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
rows.claim: Ibn Arabi says it is uncertain whether the verse means the very splitting requested by the Arabs, though the following account of their seeing a sign and calling it magic makes that the apparent reading.
rows.anchor: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî Fütûhât’ının üç yüz otuzuncu bâbında Hazret-i Muhammediyeden menzil-i Kamer’i marifet hakkında berzahî bir ifade ile şöyle der:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı explains that the Prophet need not compel belief after showing a miracle: even if the Arabs had made non-objection a condition, a coercive sign would contradict the wisdom of prophethood.
rows.anchor: mucizeyi gösterdikten sonra ilcâî bir surette inandırmak Peygamber’in vazifesi değildir. Hatta suallerinde şart etselerdi yine lâzım gelmezdi, çünkü ilcâî âyet hikmet-i bi‘sete münâfîdir

rows.speaker: Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
rows.claim: Ibn Arabi says people arriving from elsewhere reported that night's split; the deniers still called it persistent magic, and the decree that every matter reaches its settled outcome came to pass.
rows.anchor: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî Fütûhât’ının üç yüz otuzuncu bâbında Hazret-i Muhammediyeden menzil-i Kamer’i marifet hakkında berzahî bir ifade ile şöyle der:

rows.speaker: Fennî
rows.claim: Fennî reads Ibn Arabi as allowing that the split occurred only in viewers' eyes, but argues it could still be a true miracle because no sorcerer is known to project an illusion onto a celestial body.
rows.anchor: Maddiyyûn Mezhebinin İzmihlâli nâm kitabında Bay İsmail Fennî

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı rejects the proposed defense of an eye-only splitting: presenting an unreal event as real is still deception and incompatible with prophetic sanctity, and that is precisely what the deniers meant by calling it magic.
rows.anchor: Böyle bir cevap hiç de doğru olmaz. İtiraf etmek lâzım gelir ki gerek kavilde olsun gerek fiilde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says Ibn Arabi narrates the splitting as an actual event throughout; his disputed words describe the deniers' own uncertain, intermediate viewpoint, not Ibn Arabi's endorsement of an optical illusion, and 53:30 concerns those deniers.
rows.anchor: Şeyh’in anlattığı da budur. O, kelâmının bütün cereyânında inşikāk-ı Kamer’i bir vak‘a olarak anlatmıştır.

rows.speaker: Şeyh
rows.claim: Ibn Arabi says reflection and observation lead from visible things to hidden truths, with witnessing higher than thought; he connects this movement to the signs for the pious and thinkers.
rows.anchor: Onun için Şeyh o sözler arkasından şu ihtârı yapar: “Yine bil ki nazar ve itibar, esrâr ve envârdan

rows.speaker: Şeyh
rows.claim: Ibn Arabi says God teaches the pious so doubt does not enter their knowledge, while thinkers depend on fallible created powers; the thinker lies between eyesight and pure insight.
rows.anchor: Onun için Şeyh o sözler arkasından şu ihtârı yapar: “Yine bil ki nazar ve itibar, esrâr ve envârdan

rows.speaker: Fennî
rows.claim: Fennî says the majority rejects the report from Uthman b. Ata's father that the split belongs to the Resurrection, relying on Companion reports and the clear indication of 54:2, and accepts a Prophetic-era miracle.
rows.anchor: Mûmâ ileyh Fennî Bay da kelâmının sonunda hiss-i takvâsıyla basiretine sahip

rows.speaker: Fennî
rows.claim: Fennî professes that God can do all things, natural laws are only consequences of His command Be, and the Qur'an is wholly true; he therefore accepts the Moon's real splitting without hesitation, leaving its manner to God and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: Mûmâ ileyh Fennî Bay da kelâmının sonunda hiss-i takvâsıyla basiretine sahip

rows.speaker: Fennî
rows.claim: Fennî answers that people around the event and in other regions saw the Moon split; differing horizons, clouds, people indoors, and lack of sky-watching explain why it was not seen everywhere.
rows.anchor: Mûmâ ileyh Fennî Bay da kelâmının sonunda hiss-i takvâsıyla basiretine sahip

rows.speaker: Fennî
rows.claim: Fennî says the event may have gone unrecorded in that age of ignorance because people attributed it to sorcerers, jinn, or devils.
rows.anchor: Mûmâ ileyh Fennî Bay da kelâmının sonunda hiss-i takvâsıyla basiretine sahip

rows.speaker: Fennî
rows.claim: Fennî warns that reducing miracles to natural laws makes them ordinary; human reason cannot grasp the nature of supernatural events and errs when applied beyond its competence.
rows.anchor: Mûmâ ileyh Fennî Bay da kelâmının sonunda hiss-i takvâsıyla basiretine sahip

rows.speaker: Seyyid Şerîf
rows.claim: In Sharh al-Mawaqif, Sayyid Sharif calls the Moon-splitting miracle mutawatir.
rows.anchor: Şerh-i Mevâkıf’ta Seyyid Şerîf, inşikāk-ı Kamer mucizesinin mütevâtir olduğunu söylemiştir.

rows.speaker: Sübkî
rows.claim: Subki prefers the view that the splitting is mutawatir: it is explicit in the Qur'an and related through numerous routes in the Sahihayn and other collections.
rows.anchor: şerhinde Sübkî de bunu ihtiyar ederek der ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says the Qur'an explicitly establishes the event and the combined hadith corpus is widely known enough for meaningful tawatur; because tafsir details' tawatur is disputed, those who interpret or deny the details are not declared unbelievers.
rows.anchor: Tevâtürü, Kur’an’da وَٱنشَقَّ ٱلْقَمَرُ sarih olmak haysiyetiyledir.
